paper_metadata.title: Financial Portfolio Optimization: a QUBO Formulation for Sharpe Ratio Maximization

summary: The paper formulates Sharpe-ratio portfolio optimization over 432 S&P500 assets (2013–2020 data) as large QUBO problems with 3,888 binary variables for a proxy formulation and 5,184 variables for a proposed quadratic formulation, solved using D‑Wave QBSolv and D‑Wave Hybrid. Solutions are evaluated across 10 feasible runs after calibration of penalty parameters (λ₀≈1.2631 or 0.7, λ₁=300), but the study reports no explicit runtime, objective-value comparisons, or classical baseline benchmarks, so quantum advantage cannot be evaluated.

experiments.description: Sharpe Ratio proxy QUBO formulation solved with D-Wave QBSolv on S&P500 log-return portfolio data, using discretized asset weights and a penalty constraint enforcing full investment.

problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize proxy objective sum_i (mu_i/sigma_i) * sum_k d_k x_{ik} + sum_{i<j} rho_{ij} (sum_k d_k x_{ik})(sum_k d_k x_{jk})
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty term added to QUBO: (sum_i sum_k d_k x_{ik} - 1)^2 with weight lambda_1

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization over S&P500 assets using adjusted close daily prices from Yahoo Finance, with log-returns selected after Gaussianity check.
problem_instance.dataset_name: S&P500 adjusted close prices from Yahoo Finance

preprocessing: remove null values
exclude assets with consecutive null values
compute simple returns and log-returns
annualize sample mean and covariance with factor 252
remove assets with negative expected return
use log-returns based on Shapiro test

classical_preprocessing: construction of QUBO coefficients from expected returns, standard deviations, and correlations
classical_postprocessing: compute Sharpe Ratio statistics over 10 feasible solutions

convergence_data.variance_across_runs: 10 feasible solutions reported after calibration; 20 runs used in calibration appendix

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim is made for this experiment; the paper compares solution quality against a classical benchmark.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Unknown; experiment encodes a 432‑asset portfolio into a 3,888-variable QUBO solved via D‑Wave QBSolv but provides no scaling or runtime comparison against classical solvers.
